oneLiner: A university computer-vision prototype that follows movement through vehicle tracking, plate recognition and operator visualization.
summary: A five-person team project connecting OpenCV motion detection, YOLO vehicle/plate models and PaddleOCR through Python services, Redis queues and a PyQt desktop viewer. Tomer’s existing contribution statement focuses on motion detection, data preparation, model training/fine-tuning and pipeline integration. The current source supports the recognition and visualization architecture; older authorization logic and evaluation runners need separate qualification.

contribution.statement: On a five-person team, I focused on motion detection, gathering and preparing data, training and fine-tuning the recognition models, and pipeline integration.
contribution.basis: Preserved from src/content/work/systems.ts snapshot.contribution and frame/build sections; not inferred from whole-repository ownership.
contribution.independentSourceLimit: This shallow pinned revision demonstrates the team implementation but contains no training scripts or contribution map. Do not attribute every module, service, UI or model to Tomer.

architecture.note: Redis provides queue boundaries. OCR uses blocking HTTP inside the worker; callback names do not make that call asynchronous. CloudService is a local Docker CPU service, not a paid cloud inference provider.

decisions.title: Use motion as a gate before new vehicle inference.
decisions.why: The active path skips new YOLO vehicle inference when it has no motion candidates.
decisions.tradeoff: A missed motion region can suppress a useful vehicle candidate. Existing tracks can still lead to plate inference while they age out.

decisions.title: Preserve vehicle identity across frames.
decisions.why: Centroid tracking lets repeated plate crops contribute to one vehicle record instead of treating each frame independently.
decisions.tradeoff: Distance/disappearance thresholds can confuse occlusion or nearby vehicles; no tracking-quality benchmark is published.

decisions.title: Split inference and display into service boundaries.
decisions.why: Acquisition, edge processing, OCR and desktop rendering have different costs and control needs.
decisions.tradeoff: Serialization, queue backlog and synchronous OCR requests introduce extra failure and latency points; no end-to-end latency results were measured.

decisions.title: Check likely plate formats after OCR.
decisions.why: Pattern checks and look-alike substitutions reject or correct some raw OCR strings.
decisions.tradeoff: A valid format is not proof of the correct plate; generic patterns and correction order can bias ambiguous results.

decisions.title: Expose operator controls around the pipeline.
decisions.why: Loading, pausing, resuming and skipping footage support inspection of recognition behavior.
decisions.tradeoff: The current file picker and container paths need coordination; the UI updates status even when API errors are only logged.

limitations.title: No runtime or accuracy claim from this audit.
limitations.detail: Source-only review; models were not loaded, services were not started and evaluation scripts were not executed. No source-published model/end-to-end accuracy result found.

limitations.title: Unauthorized-vehicle alerts are not wired into the current service path.
limitations.detail: The current edge endpoint always calls visualize(frame, True). List authorization exists in a stale legacy path. Describe the current system as plate recognition and operator visualization, with authorization as earlier prototype logic.

limitations.title: ROI, direction classification and fusion helpers are historical/experimental.
limitations.detail: RegionAdjuster is unused by current prediction; image fusion, multiple-threshold preprocessing and weighted majority voting are defined but not called by the current OCR path.

limitations.title: Four workers share sequential model/tracker state.
limitations.detail: All workers receive one EdgeService; its prev_frame and tracker state can be touched across frames. Tracker methods lock portions of state, but EdgeService.lock is not used around prediction. Ordering and concurrency behavior need runtime evaluation.

limitations.title: Queue and network behavior are prototype-grade.
limitations.detail: The Python queue is bounded, but Redis input/output lists are not; the poller busy-loops and OCR HTTP calls have no timeout. Do not describe the complete system as fully bounded or fault tolerant.

limitations.title: Startup clears Redis globally.
limitations.detail: Both video startup and the new-architecture tester call flushall. Any future local execution must use an isolated Redis container and ports.

limitations.title: Evaluation contracts need reconciliation.
limitations.detail: New tester expects tracked_plates, but no active production caller invokes log_results; older tests import missing classes or call superseded signatures. Syntax parsing passed but does not prove tests pass.

limitations.title: Videos and reproducible training history are absent.
limitations.detail: Full videos are ignored, model weights are tracked, and this revision has no training script/configuration or held-out benchmark report. Existing user-stated training/data contribution remains valid as self-described team work; this snapshot cannot independently attribute it.

limitations.title: Desktop paths and container mounts differ.
limitations.detail: A path picked on Windows is sent directly to the service, while Compose mounts only ./recordings at /app/recordings. A future run must map/copy only authorized local fixtures.

visualConcept.title: One frame, four decisions
visualConcept.medium: Code-native SVG/CSS storyboard and architecture diagram
visualConcept.composition: A wide technical strip shows the same explicitly illustrative vehicle frame through motion contours, tracked box + ID, plate crop, and normalized character string. The strip sits above the actual service graph; a small context rail marks which stage is being explained.
visualConcept.interaction: Optional four-step buttons reveal each stage instantly; show all labels without interaction and provide a static mobile stack.
details: Use a simple authored vehicle silhouette, two offset motion contours, bounding-box coordinates and one persistent track ID.
Use a clearly fictional example plate without numerical confidence scores; label the entire strip “Pipeline illustration”.
Mark repeated observations as candidate → repeated → stable, explaining the exact higher-confidence/repetition rule in adjacent text.
Represent queue boundaries as small buffers; distinguish the HTTP crop transfer from Redis frame transport.
Do not fabricate a photographed parking scene, screenshots, real inference output, benchmark values or an operational alert.
visualConcept.suggestedCaption: Motion, tracking and character recognition form one connected path. Diagram based on the team source; no inference is running.

recommendedCorrections.change: Replace unqualified operator alerts with operator visualization. Keep authorization as historical prototype logic only.
Use Ultralytics YOLO / YOLO11 from actual model loading; README’s flow paragraph still says YOLOv8.
Say queued services, with synchronous OCR requests inside workers. Only the in-process queue is bounded.
Source and evaluation tooling are preserved; no published accuracy numbers or current passing-test assertion.

inventory.note: All tracked paths and object hashes inventoried; authored Python/config/docs fully read. Data/model/icon payloads were not semantically reviewed. Initial git object-size enumeration incidentally fetched some model objects before it was stopped; no models were checked out, loaded or executed.

citations.claim: OpenCV accepts a file/RTSP string; decoding targets four accepted frames per second with wall-clock throttling.
FastAPI video controls start, pause, resume, stop, restart and skip; worker pushes pickled frames into Redis.
Farneback optical flow produces a magnitude mask; area filtering and box merging identify motion regions.
Without new motion, vehicle inference is skipped and existing tracks age; otherwise vehicle classes, confidence, motion overlap and NMS filter detections.
Motion/vehicle matching checks an aspect-ratio range and minimum IoU.
Plate detector candidates are assigned to spatially aligned tracked vehicles, with one plate per assigned vehicle.
Centroid distance matching, disappearance counters and persistent object metadata associate detections over time.
Equal-or-higher-confidence repeated text updates a track; two subsequent same-text occurrences mark it done.
An in-process queue has maxsize30; the Redis poller drops frames when it cannot enqueue in0.1 seconds.
Four threads share the same EdgeService and motion/tracking/model state.
Plate crops are JPEG/base64 encoded and sent to a separate OCR HTTP service; response updates the track.
PaddleOCR loads local model directories on CPU; preprocessing resizes, grayscales, blurs and sharpens before selecting high-confidence text.
OCR pipeline uses resize_plate and sharpenHBF, not the other experimental fusion/thresholding/voting utilities.
Six format patterns and visually similar character mappings validate or attempt to correct plate text.
Annotated frames go to Redis visual_frame_queue; visualization is called with authorized=True unconditionally.
PyQt provides load/start/pause/resume/restart/skip controls and consumes annotated frames on a100ms timer.
Three Python services plus Redis run in Docker Compose; models and recordings are mounted from the host.
PaddleOCR2.10.0 and PaddlePaddle2.6.2 are pinned; most other dependency versions are not.
List-based authorization is implemented as a helper, not called by the current service path.
Legacy main references CarDetector/LicensePlateDetector absent from current modules and calls superseded method signatures.
RegionAdjuster is instantiated but explicitly unused in current prediction; ROI/entrance/exit helpers belong to older work.
New-architecture evaluator counts exact and optional similarity-threshold matches, then computes precision/recall/F1.
Evaluator waits for tracked_plates; EdgeService.log_results can publish that key but is not called by current production code.
Component evaluation imports a missing CarDetector and uses an old MotionDetector signature.
Video startup calls Redis flushall; this is unsafe against a shared Redis instance.
Desktop file picker sends its local path directly; containers only mount the recordings directory.
Full recordings are ignored; the README requires the user to supply a video.
